section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes psychometric evaluation of a Malay translation of the BAS-2 in a Malaysian community sample, reporting a one-dimensional factor structure supported by EFA and CFA, adequate internal consistency (omega ≥ .88), and partial invariance across sex and ethnicity. It notes that body appreciation related positively to life satisfaction and subjective happiness, showed equivocal associations with BMI (significant in women but not men), and highlights strengths (translation process, community sample) and limitations (opportunistic recruitment, limited ethnic coverage, lack of test-retest).

section_summary.extract_value: The present study examined the factor structure and psychometric properties of a Malay translation of the BAS-2 and found that Malay BAS-2 scores are best considered one-dimensional with adequate internal consistency and partial invariance across sex and ethnicity. The authors report partial sex invariance (configural and metric, but not full scalar), partial ethnic scalar invariance (Malays vs Chinese), and that body appreciation was significantly associated with BMI in women but not men; analyses were conducted on a community sample and ethnicity- and sex-specific comparisons were reported.
